OF MV ACT PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 13.01.2022 PASSED BY THE II ADDITIONAL JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, BENGALURU (SCCH-13) IN MVC NO.951/2019 DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT "Whether the Tribunal was justified in dismissing the claim petition of the appellant"?
is the question involved in this case.
2. The appellant was the claimant and the respondents were respondent Nos.1 and 2 in M.V.C.No.951/2019 on the file of MACT, SCCH-13, Bangalore.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to according to their ranks before the Tribunal.

3. On 19.11.2018 at 8.00 p.m. the claimant met with the accident opposite to City Bank,
B.T.M.Layout II Stage, Bangalore.

He filed M.V.C.No.951/2019 contending that on 19.11.2018 at 8.00 p.m. when he was crossing the road, rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HU-6362 came in high speed, rash and negligent manner hit him.
He claimed that in the accident he has suffered grievous injuries and consequent permanent physical disability.
At the relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the Insurer and registered owner of vehicle bearing No.KA-05-HU-6362.
The claimant sought compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.
4. Respondent No.2 owner of the vehicle did not contest the matter.
Respondent No.1 alone contested the matter denying the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident.
Respondent No.1 contended that the claimant in collusion with the police and other authorities have concocted the first information report, the charge sheet and other related records.
5. In support of his case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the doctor who treated him in Sparsh Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P21.
On behalf of the respondents no evidence was adduced.

6. The Tribunal on hearing the parties, by the impugned award dismissed the petition holding that the claimant's own document creates doubt about the involvement of the insured vehicle or manner of the accident.

The Tribunal further held that even assuming that the accident has taken place in Harish N Achar vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co.Ltd on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53004530/
2 the manner narrated by the claimant, the claimant was crossing the main road at the place meant for vehicular traffic and not for pedestrians.

Submissions of Smt.Suma.K., learned Counsel for the claimant:
7.
The police on investigation have filed the charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle.
On trial, the learned Magistrate convicted the rider of the motorcycle.
Respondent No.1 in his statement of objections has admitted the involvement of the vehicle of respondent No.2.
Under such circumstance, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident was not proved is unsustainable.
Having regard to the medical condition of the claimant, the Tribunal should not have attached undue importance to the delay in filing the complaint.
The impugned award suffers perversity.
8. In support of her submissions, she relies on the unreported judgment of this Court in Sri K.Lokesh vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd. & Anr.1.

entities.text: Sri K.Lokesh vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd. & Anr.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Submissions of Sri B.C.Shivanne Gowda, learned Counsel for the Insurer:
9. The police records or the conviction of the rider of the motorcycle is not conclusive proof for MACT in a M.F.A.No.8348/2012 c/w M.F.A.No.6845/2012 DD 11.11.2020 proceeding under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act').
The claimant's own documents were mutually inconsistent and self contradictory going to the root of the matter.
Neither the eyewitnesses nor the complainant were examined before the Tribunal or in criminal case.
The evidence on record clearly shows that all such documents were got up in collusion with respondent No.2, the claimant, police and other authorities.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in dismissing the petition.
There is no illegality or perversity in the order.

10. In support of his submissions, he relies on the following judgments:
(i) Veerappa v. Siddappa2  (ii) Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. v.
 Ashok Raja Urs.K3.

sentences.text: It is no doubt true that on the complaint of the son of the claimant as per Ex.P2, the first information report as per Ex.P1 was registered against the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HU-6362 in Crime No.59/2018 of Mico Layout Traffic Police Station.
On investigation the charge sheet as per Ex.P9 was filed against him which culminated in C.C.No.986/2019 on the file of the Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court-IV, Bangalore.

In that case, the said Court by Harish N Achar vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co.Ltd on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53004530/
3 judgment dated 05.03.2019 convicted one Avinash Sahay/accused for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC and Section 187 of the MV Act and sentenced him to fine of Rs.1,000/- for each of the offences under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC and fine of Rs.500/- for the offence punishable under Section 187 of the MV Act.

sentences.text: 12. But the question is whether such records of the criminal case become ultimatum for the Courts in the proceeding under Section 166 of the MV Act and whether the Court is bound by those documents and cannot traverse beyond that.

In that connection the coordinate Bench of this Court in Veerappa's case referred to supra taking judicial note of the unholy alliance of police, doctors,
lawyers, sometime even the Insurance Company, in para 16 of the judgment held as follows:
" 16.
Sub - Section (2) of Section 149 provides the grounds on which the insurance company can avoid the liability to pay the compensation under the Act.
One such ground is, if a policy is obtained by a representation of fact which was false in some material particular.

Section 172 confers on the Claims Tribunal a power to award compensatory costs, if it is satisfied that the policy of insurance is void on the ground that it was obtained by representation of fact which was false in any material particular or any party or insured has put forward a false or vexatious claim or defence.
Sub- Section (3) of Section 172 also speaks of criminal liability in respect of such misrepresentation.
However, it restricts the compensatory costs to be awarded to only Rs.1,000/-.
Therefore, the Act provides for taking action against a party who sets up a false or vexatious defence.
However, the cost of Rs.1,000/- prescribed under the aforesaid provision, has failed to act as a sufficient deterrent to the parties setting up false claim or defence.
The experience has shown that this branch of law is slowly getting into the hands of unscrupulous people who are making a mockery of judicial process.
A disturbing trend of unholy alliance among the police, the doctors, the lawyers and some times even the Insurance Company, to siphon out the public money, and make an unlawful gain is fast emerging.
It is also gaining respectability and persons who indulge in such practices are acclaimed as most successful in their respective profession.
This is a dangerous trend, if unchecked would undermine the judicial process.
As the existing law is inadequate to check this malady, the Court not only have to be careful in adjudicating such claims but also find ways to prevent such abuse.

They have to balance the interest of these accident victims and their legal heirs on one side, by giving them just compensation at the earliest, thus giving effect to the mandate of the parliament, and on the other hand, to see that the very process is not abused and exploited by a handful of persons, who have attained specialization in this field, to make personal gains at the cost of the exchequer.
An onerous responsibility lies on the Courts.

Therefore, it is imperative that a strong message is to be sent to the abusers of the judicial process to discourage them from indulging in such practices as well as the consequences of such abuse may result in foisting the liability exclusively on the insured-owner of the vehicle."
(Emphasis supplied)

sentences.text: This Court in Mahadevi's case referred to supra held that when fraud and collusion is pleaded by the Insurer, it is not bound to challenge the charge sheet.
It was further held that without challenging the validity of the charge sheet, the Insurer can take all such plea in the proceedings before the MACT.
It is further observed that mere charge sheet if deficient in truth cannot prevent the Court from weighing other evidence on record.

14. In B.C.Kumar's case referred to supra, this Court held that even where the driver pleaded guilty that does not bar MACT from considering the other evidence on record, but to examine whether the accident occurred as painted by the claimant in involving the insured vehicle.

15. Reading of the above judgments makes it clear that the police records or even the plea of guilt by the rider of the vehicle does not bar the Court from assessing the evidence independently in the proceeding under Section 166 of the MV Act.

In the light of such legal position, this Court has to examine whether the Tribunal appreciated the evidence properly in arriving at the conclusion that the claimant has failed to prove that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HU-6362.
16.
According to the claimant, the accident took place on 19.11.2018 at 8.00 p.m.
Ex.P1 shows that the complaint was filed on 24.11.2018 at 11.00 a.m. Soon after the accident, according to the claimant himself, he was taken to Gangothri Hospital.
The complaint was filed by the son of the claimant.
He was not the eyewitness.

In the complaint, he says that on that day at 8.00 p.m. one Sudeep after - 10 - admission of his father in Gangothri Hospital informed him over phone about the accident and admission of his father in the hospital.
For the first time in the said complaint, bike involving registration No. KA-05-HU-6362 was stated.
Even in that complaint the name of the rider was not stated.
Soon after the accident, the claimant said to have been taken to Gangothri Hospital.
The entire medical records of Sparsh Hospital and Department of Neuro Surgery in Sparsh Hospital and prescription issued by Gangothri hospital are together marked at Ex.P18.

The prescription of Gangothri Hospital on 19.11.2018 issued at 11.35 p.m. states that the claimant was brought with history of road traffic accident at BTM Layout, hit by two wheeler near City Bank, BTM Layout.
Neither the vehicle number nor the name of the rider was mentioned in that.
In Ex.P18 the history showed in Sparsh Hospital is RTA "Pedestrian vs. two wheeler".
17. In Ex.P4 the police intimation issued by Sparsh Hospital, history was written as 25.11.2018 and that is altered as 19.11.2018 at 8.00 p.m.
In Ex.P18 internal page 21 of the record, history is mentioned as road traffic accident when he was sitting on his parked bike which was hit by two - 11 - wheeler near City Bank, BTM Layout.
There is some scoring of the word pedestrian and words "sitting on the bike" are interpolated.

In discharge summary Ex.P18 at internal page 12 history is Harish N Achar vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co.Ltd on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53004530/
5 mentioned as "presented with alleged history of road traffic accident (pedestrian vs. two wheeler)".
18.

sentences.text: Therefore that document prevails over Ex.P18.
The claimant cannot approbate and reprobate simultaneously asking the Court to accept one part of the document and discard another part of the document which incriminates against him.

In similar situation in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Premlata Shukla7, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in para 13 of the judgment held as follows:
"13.

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Premlata Shukla7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the factum of an accident could also be proved from the first information report.

It is also to be noted that once a part of the contents of the document is admitted in evidence, the party bringing the same on record cannot be permitted to turn round and contend that the other contents contained in the rest part thereof had not been proved.
Both the parties have relied thereupon.
It was marked as an exhibit as both the parties intended to rely upon them."

(Emphasis supplied) (2007) 13 SCC 476 - 12 - 19. In para 14 of the aforesaid judgment it was held that, once a part of the document relied upon by both parties, the Tribunal cannot be said to have committed illegality in relying upon the other part irrespective of the contents of the documents having been proved or not.
20. In this case, the said document Ex.P18 was proved by the claimant himself by examining PW.2.

Therefore he cannot resile from the contents of the document which did not suit him or which go against his case.
21.
So far as the judgment in C.C.No.986/2019, on close scrutiny that reveals shocking deviation from the judicial norms.
In that case, the prosecution neither examined the complainant nor the eyewitnesses.
That judgment says on examination of the Investigating Officer, the prosecution gave up all other witnesses.
Relying on the version of the Investigating Officer who was neither the eyewitness nor the complainant or injured, the Magistrate proceeded to convict the accused.
Probably the accused therein was complacent because it was only sentence of fine.
Therefore, he did not challenge that.

Analysis of over all materials on record shows that there is force in the contention of respondent No.1 that there was collusion between the complainant, the claimant, the police and respondent No.2 and the alleged accused in C.C.No.986/2019.
23.
Reading of the judgment in K.Lokesh's case referred to supra relied upon by learned Counsel for the claimant shows that in that case the victim of the accident was unconscious for one month.
Therefore, this Court held that delay in filing of the complaint was acceptable one.
The said judgment is not applicable to the facts of the present case.

sentences.text: Aforesaid facts and circumstances and the judgments go to show that the Tribunal on sound appreciation of the evidence, acting in accordance with established principles of law has arrived at the conclusion that the claimant has failed to prove the involvement of the insured vehicle in the case.
If at all any body has to be penalized, it is respondent No.2 who was the active party to fraud and collusion.
Therefore, he shall be penalized.
The appeal is liable - 14 - to be dismissed imposing heavy costs on respondent No.2.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.

Respondent No.2 shall pay costs of Rs.50,000/- to the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority within two weeks from the date of release of this judgment failing which the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is entitled to recover the same as land revenue.
Communicate copy of this judgment to the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
